Bound for Glory - We've Got Your Number - [4:17]
Introducing Super X OS: A new Ubuntu based distro focused on ease of use and good presentation
Default DE: KDE w/ custom theme and modified homerun launcher.

I like these initiatives since it promotes the idea of freedom with Linux. You want something? You build it. However in reality the killer is always staying power. It's hard to recommend options that are unlikely to stick around.

There's a bit of a catch 22 situation. This is a new distro that will evolve all the time, yet is "aimed towards beginners, casual users and businesses looking for a well supported user-friendly OS." I'm not sure quite how much these users enjoy constant updates and partially broken things. Therefore it's likely to be power users that pick this up and they are less likely to be blown away by fancy graphics.

I wish people with this skill would work on refining/creating DEs that are user friendly, instead of whole distros.

That said this could be a good thing if they borrow heavily from the great Ubuntu installer. There's something to be said for a great out of the box experience - I just worry that it can't be done with a team this size (of mostly designers...).

Interesting that they have paid options even though they seem somewhat naive.

$5 a year gets you:

>-10 On Site Support calls*

>-Unlimited Phone Support

>-Unlimited Email Support

>*On Site support is available only in Guwahati, Assam (India) and adjoining areas.

BONUS: It has the cube from 2003

From what I can tell, it's a company and distro made by an Indian High School student. I've played around with it myself, and I was fairly impressed to be honest. It's a well put together idea of what I naturally do with Kubuntu out of the box. (aside from a few bugs of course)

My concern is not with the product, but more that they seem to be targeting a group of people who are not keen on patches and updates. I only manage IT for a relatively small group, but the attitude on updates and bug fixes is always AVOID AVOID. These are going to be key in a new-ish project such as this one.

They do have some interesting ideas on rolling it out to enterprise though, and their support packages are a good deal. Good luck to them I say, but it's a though nut to crack.
